note: The almanac of Boon.land — wonders a reader can collect (book/scripts/modules/almanac.mjs). Canon: .spw/surfaces/almanac.spw. `terms` are matched in the prose, case-insensitively; `home` is where each is first met, `echoes` where it returns.

wonders.name: Torch-ants
wonders.note: Keep lit streets along the berry roots all winter, so the field never freezes through. Businesslike; very particular about torches.
wonders.hint: Something keeps the field warm from underneath.

wonders.name: Echo-wrens
wonders.note: Small brown wrens that sing a beat late. They nest in hollow cedars; a wren-call is the grove saying again.
wonders.hint: A bird in the grove that is always a little behind.

wonders.name: The lag-stag
wonders.note: A white stag nobody has seen. Its hoofprints press into the moss a beat after it has passed.
wonders.hint: Prints in the grove, with nothing to make them.

wonders.name: Rehearsal moths
wonders.note: Dusk moths whose wings carry tomorrow’s weather, a little smudged. The grove keeps its almanac on them.
wonders.hint: Wings that know the weather early.

wonders.name: Salt-whales
wonders.note: Vast, slow creatures under the salt flats. The flats are the roof of their road; their old roads glow under the crust.
wonders.hint: Something enormous moves under the flats.

wonders.name: Signal-skinks
wonders.note: Finger-long lizards that bask on the signal stones and flick their tails in a code only the stones answer.
wonders.hint: Small tails, flicking a message on warm stones.

wonders.name: The weathercocks
wonders.note: Iron roosters of Council Hill that vote by turning. The crosswind is their disagreement made weather.
wonders.hint: Iron that turns with an opinion.

wonders.name: Hum-crickets
wonders.note: Live in the Rift’s crack and keep its pitch. They go silent when someone lies near the floor.
wonders.hint: A small chorus that lives in a crack.

wonders.name: Pane-snails
wonders.note: Glass-snails that graze soot off Bonk City’s panes at night. Their slow trails are how a pane is forgiven clear.
wonders.hint: Something cleans the city’s glass by night.

wonders.name: Gate-pigeons
wonders.note: Sleep on the parcel gate’s counterweight and ride it up and down all night without waking.
wonders.hint: Birds that sleep on something moving.

wonders.name: Oath-moths
wonders.note: Grey market moths drawn to sworn words. They settle in the oath groove only when a promise is true.
wonders.hint: Moths that can tell a true promise.

wonders.name: Remembrancers
wonders.note: Pale fish in the Watering Eye that swim through the faces the well has kept, folding them gently so they fit.
wonders.hint: Something swims among the faces in the well.

wonders.name: Jazz-geese
wonders.note: Geese that fly in nines and honk in uneven time. One of them taught the Fool his note, or the other way round.
wonders.hint: A honk with a swing to it.

wonders.name: Chimney-swifts
wonders.note: Roost in the ridge chimneys and carry a sound a little farther than it meant to go.
wonders.hint: Birds that carry sound.

wonders.name: Load-beetles
wonders.note: Small dark beetles in Bone.land timber that click when a beam is asked to bear more than it agreed to.
wonders.hint: A click in the timber, when something is too heavy.

wonders.name: Crown-wasps
wonders.note: Build paper crowns in the bloom garden, beautiful and hollow. A rented crown is wasp-work.
wonders.hint: Somebody builds crowns out of paper.

wonders.name: Early bees
wonders.note: Arrive at a flower before it opens and wait, humming, as if the bloom owed them.
wonders.hint: Bees that come before the flowers.

wonders.name: Seam-otters
wonders.note: Swim exactly on the unblended seam of the two rivers, one paw in each water.
wonders.hint: Something swims on the line between two waters.

wonders.name: Ink-herons
wonders.note: Stand in the berry-dark river so still their reflections dry into the bank.
wonders.hint: Birds so still their reflections stay.

wonders.name: Shelf-owls
wonders.note: Keep the gaps in the archive’s shelves clear for chronicles not yet written. They nest in what is missing.
wonders.hint: Someone guards the empty places on the shelves.

wonders.name: Hob-deer
wonders.note: Deer no taller than a boot that graze between frost-ruts only on days nobody keeps.
wonders.hint: Small deer of a day nobody kept.

wonders.name: The page-fox
wonders.note: A fox the colour of an unturned page, seen only on unkept days, trotting as if late for something.
wonders.hint: A pale fox, on a day nobody kept.

wonders.name: Press-stones
wonders.note: The archivist’s flat stones for holding a map’s crease. One is always missing.
wonders.hint: Weights for a map that will not lie flat.

wonders.name: The drying-line
wonders.note: Where new maps hang to dry. Maps that refuse ink drip back into the trough.
wonders.hint: Where maps hang, waiting.

wonders.name: The want-needle
wonders.note: The Genie’s brass needle, quick to find a want. It circles, slows, and tries again.
wonders.hint: A needle that points at wanting.

wonders.name: The resolution glass
wonders.note: The Genie’s long glass. It shows only wants larger than a loaf.
wonders.hint: A glass that cannot see small things.

wonders.name: The wish-scale
wonders.note: The Genie’s pan scale, balanced against coincidences.
wonders.hint: A scale for the price of a wish.

wonders.name: The bottle-desk
wonders.note: The folding desk the Genie keeps in his bottle, with a drawer for Thursdays.
wonders.hint: A whole office, folded small.

wonders.name: The key-file bench
wonders.note: Where keys are filed smaller, never grown. The filings go into a jar called the honest jar.
wonders.hint: A bench where keys only get smaller.

wonders.name: The crosswind loom
wonders.note: Weaves the hill’s two winds into the council’s tablecloth. When the vote turns, the weave changes colour.
wonders.hint: A loom worked by weather.

wonders.name: The crack-gauge
wonders.note: Brass calipers set across the Rift’s crack. They measure in notes, not inches.
wonders.hint: Calipers that measure a sound.

wonders.name: The bonk-kiln
wonders.note: The forgiving kiln of Bonk City. It melts old impacts down into clear glass.
wonders.hint: Where the city’s bruises become glass.

wonders.name: Dent-lanterns
wonders.note: Lanterns hammered from dented brass. Each dent is a street the light remembers.
wonders.hint: Lanterns that remember being struck.

wonders.name: Chime-gutters
wonders.note: Gutters that ring when it rains, so the city can hear which roofs are leaking.
wonders.hint: The city listens to its rain.

wonders.name: Lamp-ladders
wonders.note: The lamplighters’ hinged ladders that fold into a walking staff.
wonders.hint: A ladder that becomes a staff.

wonders.name: The folio press
wonders.note: Glasses a page flat and warm, layering it over the last so nothing known is lost.
wonders.hint: A press for keeping pages under glass.

wonders.name: Brace-boxes
wonders.note: Small glass boxes with sigil-etched lids. Each holds a pocket realm combined from two nouns and a sigil, and runs on borrowed warmth.
wonders.hint: Small boxes that hold small weathers.

wonders.name: Pie-dividers
wonders.note: Brass compasses for dividing a pie evenly. They never come out even.
wonders.hint: An instrument that cannot quite divide.

wonders.name: The oath-scale
wonders.note: Weighs the fruit an oath is paid in. It ignores the hand that pays.
wonders.hint: A scale that weighs promises in fruit.

wonders.name: The well-winch
wonders.note: On still nights the bucket comes up holding a face instead of water.
wonders.hint: A winch that sometimes brings up the wrong thing.

wonders.name: The shard-rack
wonders.note: The Fool’s rack for the nine honk shards. One slot is egg-shaped.
wonders.hint: A rack with one strangely shaped slot.

wonders.name: The listening mallet
wonders.note: BoneWAP’s felt-headed mallet for asking a beam what it will bear.
wonders.hint: A mallet made for asking, not striking.

wonders.name: Load-bells
wonders.note: Small bells hung from Bone.land’s joists that ring when weight passes over.
wonders.hint: Bells that ring under weight.

wonders.name: Rail-pins
wonders.note: Brass pins on the confluence bridge where receipts are posted for any traveller to read.
wonders.hint: Where the bridge keeps its notices.

wonders.name: The ferry-bell
wonders.note: Rung when someone needs to cross the seam without wetting both springs.
wonders.hint: A bell for crossing between two waters.

wonders.name: The glassing press
wonders.note: The archive’s great press for folios. It has pressed every page but the last.
wonders.hint: A press that has never pressed one page.

wonders.name: The storm-weight
wonders.note: The parcel gate’s iron counterweight. It lets one porter lift a gate meant for three.
wonders.hint: Iron that makes one person strong enough.

wonders.name: The door-rule
wonders.note: The carpenter’s folding rule, with a hinge for every size of door.
wonders.hint: A rule that folds to fit any door.

wonders.name: The council slab: &[boon, bane]{table}
wonders.note: Two sides, one table: the council’s law cut into the pine before any argument starts. Confluence without whitening.
wonders.hint: A law written in braces on a hilltop.

wonders.name: Pane faces: # and .
wonders.note: Glaziers etch # on a pane’s street face, the face that travels, and . on the inside face, the one that stays.
wonders.hint: Two marks on every pane.

wonders.name: Mortise marks: ^ and .
wonders.note: Joiners cut ^ where a beam lifts and . where it stands. A frame can be read before it is leaned on.
wonders.hint: Marks a joiner reads before trusting a beam.

wonders.name: The open brace
wonders.note: The archive files every record as a small realm in braces. The blank last line is an open brace with no close.
wonders.hint: A brace nobody has closed.

wonders.name: Hearth-drift: {frost & hearth}
wonders.note: A combine: frost and hearth in one room. It snows warm. The warm furrow is one the land made by itself.
wonders.hint: Snow that falls warm.

wonders.name: Moonrun: <river ~ moon>
wonders.note: A combine: a passage where water is thinking about being light. You can go through it; you cannot stay.
wonders.hint: A passage made of river and moonlight.
